title: The Silver Hand: The First and the Fallen

texts.details:
Now the hardest of the graves.

Uther the Lightbringer was the first of us. Faol's apprentice; the first knight ever to be called paladin. He trained a prince. Arthas Menethil was inducted into our order in the very cathedral you are standing in, and Uther loved him as a son.

When the plague came, the prince asked him to help butcher a city. Uther refused. And Arthas said: "I hereby relieve you of your command and suspend your paladins from service." With those words our order ceased to exist in law. Not long after, at Andorhal, he killed Uther with his own hand.

Go to the tomb, in the Western Plaguelands. There are knights of the order nearby whom the Scourge raised. One is Sir Thomas. Free him.
texts.objectives: Go to Uther's Tomb on Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands and lay Sir Thomas the Risen to rest nearby. Return to Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker at the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind.
texts.progress: The tomb, and then the knight. He will be close to it. They always are.
texts.completion:
You have stood where the first of us lies, and freed one of his knights.

Think on Arthas, $N. He was not a monster when he took the oath. He was the best of us. He fell because he could not bear to lose, and so he decided that the end would excuse the means. Then he decided it again. That is all it took.

Every paladin carries that door inside him. Uther's stone says that so long as we honor his example, his light shall never fade. Honor it by refusing the order Arthas gave, every time someone gives it to you.

You have earned proper plate. Choose. One grave remains.

idea: The Silver Hand, level 50: from the wiki, Uther was the first paladin; Arthas was inducted into the order, suspended it when Uther refused the culling of Stratholme ("I hereby relieve you of your command and suspend your paladins from service"), and killed Uther at Andorhal; some fallen paladins became death knights. Invented: Sir Thomas.
